messages:
oncall-bot: 🚨 Incident detected: multiple pods in inference-pool-us-east-2 marked NotReady and restarting. Pod restarts and OOM/CUDA errors observed. Auto-escalation to #eng-oncall. thread: 1867894321

oncall-bot: Alert details: 60% of gp-inference pods in pool 'gp-us-east-2-a' NotReady, 5xx rate on hosted API up from 0.2% -> 6% in last 3m. See logs and pod names below.

alex: I'm on it. pulling kubectl now. anyone on infra? @maria?

maria: here. seeing kubelet chatter on the nodes: kubelet restarted on ip-10-0-12-45 about 2m ago. probable kernel OOM or driver crash. grabbing node logs.

alex: can you paste the pod status?

maria: ```
NAME                                 READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
gp-infer-7f6d5c9b9-2xkzq             0/1     CrashLoopBackOff   7         1h
gp-infer-7f6d5c9b9-8vplm             0/1     OOMKilled          3         47m
gp-infer-7f6d5c9b9-cfjr2             1/1     Running            0         15m
```

maria: node logs show repeated: "kubelet: container runtime error: failed to allocate device memory: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY" then kubelet restarted due to keepalive failure.

alex: that matches what the inference runtime reported: CUDA driver returning device lost shortly before OOM. Could be a driver hang on that node. Which nodes impacted?

maria: nodes: ip-10-0-12-45, ip-10-0-12-46. ip-10-0-12-45 has kernel messages: "NMI watchdog: BUG: soft lockup - CPU#2 stuck for 23s" and nvidia-smi shows processes stuck with zombie GPU allocations.

infra-bot: Suggested action: cordon ip-10-0-12-45 and drain safely, then cycle the node's NVIDIA driver. Command: `kubectl cordon ip-10-0-12-45 && kubectl drain ip-10-0-12-45 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force`

alex: doing cordon+drain now, starting with ip-10-0-12-45. I'll set a 5m parallel drain on the second node only if capacity allows.

jess: heads-up: customer SLA alerts triggered for 3 enterprise customers (cs-ticket: INC-4412 INC-4419). Notifying CS to patch customers. Visible symptom: 503 on embed endpoint.

alex: drain started: pods evicted, some restarted on other nodes. watching crash loops. if crash loops persist after drain, we should fallback routing to lower-capacity model variants for affected routes.

maria: after drain and kubelet restart on ip-10-0-12-45, node rejoined but nvidia-smi still showing stale processes; will sudo systemctl restart nvidia-docker and unload/load driver modules. scheduling a reboot if that doesn't clear.

david: adding mitigation: increase fallback capacity by scaling gp-infer-smol replica set by +3 to absorb traffic for now. `kubectl scale deployment gp-infer-smol --replicas=8 -n inference`

alex: scaled gp-infer-smol. traffic shifted, 5xx rate dropped to ~1.1% over last 2m. still above baseline but improved.

maria: executed driver reload and reboot on ip-10-0-12-45. node came back Ready. observed kernel OOM killer logs targeted at a user process (cuda-worker). adding kernel parameter guard for next boot.

sre_lead: good. next steps: (1) keep node cordoned until we confirm no recurrence for 15m; (2) run health-checks and load tests on the node; (3) keep fallback routing until pool is healthy. Also open a post-incident ticket to track driver versions and kernel upgrade plan.

ops-manager: priority = P1 until 1867895040. CS informed. If we see repeat on ip-10-0-12-46, escalate to Infra Eng for hardware swap.

alex: handoff notes for next oncall: root cause suspected: driver/driver+kernel interaction causing GPU memory leaks -> GPU allocation failures -> process OOMs -> kubelet restart. Actions taken: cordon+drain ip-10-0-12-45, driver reload, node reboot, scaled fallback replicas, temporary routing to lower capacity model variants, notified CS. Monitor for 30m.

maria: logs and artifacts uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-incidents/1867894321-nodeflap/gpu-logs.tar.gz and k8s events exported.

oncall-bot: Incident status: mitigation in progress. Current impact: degraded embeddings/serve latency with transient 5xx for some customers. Next update in 10m or on major change.

jess: adding note: billing and usage impacted for affected customers; flagging for finance review if this crosses threshold.

alex: cool. leaving channel to monitor. tagging @david for 1h handoff at 1867894921.

david: taking over monitoring. will escalate to infra if another OOM appears on ip-10-0-12-46.

oncall-bot: Thread closed for now; reopen if new errors surface."
